passage: Come, Vinita, sit. Old Rafiq was a boy of ten once, and I nearly made a big mistake. My friend Salim whispered that his sister's wedding had been called off, and no neighbour knew yet. Oh, that secret sat on my tongue like hot jalebi! I wanted to tell just one person, my cousin Aslam. I walked to his gate twice. Then I thought, trust is like a glass bangle; drop it once and no glue can mend it. So I went home and drank water instead. Years later Salim told me he had never worried, because I was the one who kept my word. And if I had slipped, I would have gone to him that same evening and said sorry.

qa.q: What secret did Salim whisper to Rafiq?
qa.a: That his sister's wedding had been called off, and no neighbour knew yet.

qa.q: What was Rafiq feeling as he walked to Aslam's gate twice?
qa.a: A strong itch to tell, since the secret sat on his tongue like hot jalebi, but he also held back and thought about how fragile trust is.

qa.q: What would Rafiq have done if he had slipped and told Aslam?
qa.a: He would have gone to Salim that same evening, owned up and said sorry.

qa.q: How might Salim have felt about Rafiq keeping his word?
qa.a: Salim says he never worried, so he likely felt safe and trusting with Rafiq.

grounding: A child is tempted to pass on a juicy secret, reminds himself that trust is fragile, keeps it, and says he would have owned up and apologised if he had slipped.

passage:
Hostel warden's note, Thursday.
Jatin confided in Nilesh this week that his family is moving to another city at the end of term. He asked Nilesh not to tell anyone yet.
Tonight I heard Nilesh in the corridor, whispering, "I know something big about Jatin..." to another boy. He stopped halfway, then said, "Never mind."
Later, Nilesh came to me, looking troubled. He said he'd almost told, and had actually told one boy yesterday. I suggested he own up. He went to Jatin straight away and apologised. Jatin was upset, but they talked for a long time. I'll keep an eye on both boys.

qa.q: What secret did Jatin share with Nilesh?
qa.a: That his family is moving to another city at the end of term.

qa.q: How was Nilesh feeling when he came to the warden?
qa.a: Nilesh looked troubled and guilty about almost telling and having told one boy.

qa.q: What did Nilesh do after he slipped?
qa.a: He owned up to Jatin and apologised instead of hiding it.

qa.q: How might Jatin feel when Nilesh apologises?
qa.a: Jatin was upset that his secret got out, but Nilesh's honesty let them talk it through.

grounding: A boy is tempted to share a friend's big secret, slips once, then owns up and apologises, showing trust is fragile.

passage:
Saturday
Baljeet told me the BIGGEST secret today. Her family is adopting a baby girl next month! She said, "Don't tell anyone yet. Mama wants to wait until the papers are done."
I was bursting all afternoon. At tuition, Rinku asked, "Why are you smiling?" and the words were right there on my tongue.
But I thought about how Baljeet looked when she told me, so happy and so worried. If I told, I couldn't take it back.
So I said, "Nothing. Just a good day."
It was SO hard. But I feel proud now, like I'm someone who can be trusted.
Vasudha

qa.q: What is Baljeet's family doing next month?
How did Vasudha feel when Rinku asked about the smile?
qa.a: Vasudha felt bursting with excitement and tempted to tell.

qa.q: What helped Vasudha keep the secret?
qa.a: Remembering how happy and worried Baljeet looked, and knowing a told secret cannot be taken back.

qa.q: How might Baljeet feel if she knew Vasudha kept it?
qa.a: Baljeet would feel relieved and trust Vasudha even more.

grounding: Vasudha is desperate to share a friend's exciting secret but remembers trust is fragile and keeps it.
